**優雅**OVERVIEW   
DESCRIPTION 

\-   
IEEE VICTORIS 4.0 is an event organized by IEEE Mansoura Student Branch and powered  by the National Telecom Regulatory Authority (NTRA) to foster innovation, collaboration,  and excellence in technology. 

\-   
The event includes competitions, mentorships, and interactive sessions designed to  enhance participants' technical expertise and problem-solving abilities. 

\-   
Participants will engage in hands-on challenges and real-world projects, applying their  theoretical knowledge to gain practical experience. 

\-   
The focus on teamwork, leadership, and professional development aims to empower  participants and inspire future technological leaders. 

COMPETITION  

\-   
IEEE VICTORIS 4.0 includes various competitions, with one of its highlights being  CodeRefine — a software engineering contest where teams “rescue” broken systems. 

\-   
Teams receive buggy, inefficient codebases and must debug, refactor, optimize, and  deliver polished, high performance applications. 

\-   
Section 2 details the CodeRefine Competition. 

![][image1]1  
ELIGIBILITY  

*The competition is open to teams that meet the following requirements:* 

\-   
All team members must be currently enrolled students of 15 years old or above.  \-   
Participants must comply with all rules and regulations set forth by the competition  organizers. 

COMPETITION DETAILS **優雅**COMPETITION   
DURATION 

\-   
The competition will last for approximately 30 days, with specific dates communicated to  participants in advance. 

\-   
The competition will consist of multiple stages, each with its own timeline and deadlines. ![][image2]2  
LOCATION  

\-   
Initial stages will be conducted virtually on specified online platforms. 

\-   
The final stage will be held offline at Mansoura University, allowing participants to showcase  their work in a physical setting. 

\-   
Details of the location or online platforms will be communicated in advance. 

AWARDS 

\-   
Certificates will be awarded to qualified teams, and financial prizes will be awarded to  top-performing teams. 

 COMMUNICATION    
CHANNELS 

\-   
Official communication channels will be established for efficient information exchange. \-  
Participants will receive contact details for addressing questions or concerns.

**優雅**   
RULES *&* CODE    
OF CONDUCT 

 RULES  

\-   
All code must be written by the team during the competition window. \-   
Using AI tools (e.g., ChatGPT), search engines for code snippets, or help from anyone  outside your team is strictly prohibited. 

\-   
Any cheating, plagiarism, or rule breaking will result in immediate disqualification. \-   
Teams must not attempt to hack, modify, or interfere with the judging or testing systems. 

 CODE OF CONDUCT 

\-   
Participants are expected to uphold fairness, respect, and professionalism. \-  
Cheating, plagiarism, or unethical behavior will result in immediate disqualification. 

![][image4]4   
**優雅**   
SUBMISSION GUIDELINES 

INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY \-   
Participants retain ownership of their intellectual property but grant the organizers  non-exclusive rights to showcase their work for promotional purposes. 

FINAL REPORT 

\-   
No final report is required. 

\-   
For the final system challenge, teams must upload their complete solution to a public  GitHub repository. 

\-  
The repo must include a README that clearly explains: 

 \- What the system does 

 \- What issues were fixed and how 

 \- How to build, run, and test the project 

\-   
Judges will review your code and README directly on GitHub 

![][image5]5   
SUBMISSION    
DEADLINE 

\-   
All early problems and the GitHub link for the final problem must be submitted before the  competition period ends. 

\-   
Late submissions will not be accepted or judged. 

**優雅**DESCRIPTION   
CODE REFINE 

\-   
CodeRefine is a unique software engineering competition where participants are chal lenged to rescue broken codebases. Instead of starting from scratch, teams receive mal functioning, inefficient systems and must fix, refactor, and optimize them into clean,  high-quality solutions. 

\-   
This competition mirrors the real-world software lifecycle, where engineers often work on  maintaining and enhancing legacy code rather than creating new projects. 

![][image6]6  
OBJECTIVES 

\-   
Strengthen debugging, refactoring, and optimization skills. 

\-   
Gain hands-on experience with maintaining and improving existing codebases. \-   
Practice clean code principles and professional-grade development. 

\-   
Compete in a realistic, high-pressure environment that mirrors real tech jobs. \-   
Learn how to analyze, design, and deliver complete system improvements. 

TARGET AUDIENCE  

\-   
High school and university students with experience in one of the following programming  languages: C++, Java, Python, JavaScript, or C\#ز   
**優雅**TEAM FORMATION   
TEAMS & WORKSPACE

\-   
Teams may consist of 1 to 3 members, and interdisciplinary collaboration is encouraged. \-   
A mandatory Team Leader will coordinate activities and serve as the primary contact. \-   
It is encouraged for team members to collaborate and support each other across roles,  fostering an environment of knowledge sharing and collective problem-solving. 

![][image7]7   
**優雅**PHASE STRUCTURE   
TIMELINE & PHASES 

\-   
First phase will be the registration form to know more about which programming  language you will use during the competition. 

\-   
The competThe competition itself consists of: 

 \- Online Technical Sessions: Community learning. 

 \- Online Qualification: A 3-hours online competition designed to evaluate and select the   top-performing teams advancing to the final stage.  

 \- Offline Finals: A 5-hours in person competition where the top qualifying teams compete to   determine the competition’s top three winners. 

\-   
Each solved problem is scored instantly and your live ranking updates in real time. \-   
The final hour is a blind hour: the leaderboard is frozen; final ranks are revealed at the  award ceremony. 

DURATION AND    
COMMUNICATION 

\-   
The duration of each phase will be communicated during orientation. Teams must adhere  to the timeline and deadline. 

\-  
Clear communication channels will be established for updates and instructions 

![][image8]8   
\-   
By following the defined phase structure and timeline, teams can effectively manage their  time, allocate resources, and make steady progress towards the successful completion of  the competition. 

EVALUATION CRITERIA **優雅**& AND JUDGING EVALUATION    
\-   
Early problems: Correctness (passes test cases), 

 performance (meets time/memory limits). 

\-  
Final problem: 

 \- Functionality (meets requirements) 

 \- Code Quality (readable, well structured, maintainable)  

 \- Optimization (performance improvements) 

 \- README Clarity (explains fixes, setup, and usage)  

 \- Creativity & Scalability (smart design choices) 

![][image9]9   
JUDGING   
SYSTEM  

\-   
Automated Testing for early problems via the online platform, where each test case is  worth 1 point (e.g., a problem with 20 test cases \= 20 points; passing 5 cases \= 5 points).  The live scoreboard remains visible until the blind hour. 

\-   
Expert Review for the final problem: judges manually inspect your GitHub repo and  README. 

\-   
Final score \= sum of automated scores (early problems) \+ judge score (final problem). \-   
All judges’ decisions are final and binding. 

RESULTS    
ANNOUNCEMENT 

\-   
Results will be announced on the final competition day after the evaluations. \-   
Scores will be compiled, and winners will be determined based on overall performance. \-   
Participants will be notified of the results publicly during the final day. For any further inquiries, don’t hesitate to contact us: support@ieeemansb.org.
